= Dynamic HEIC format fixture

`synthetic-all-properties.heic` is a four-image, 8 by 8 HEIC used to establish
the RFD 4 format contract before adding the production parser. Its images are
solid red, green, blue, and white in zero-based top-level collection order.
Only image 0 is primary and carries XMP metadata.

The fixture is generated entirely from `generate.c`; it contains no third-party
artwork. The generator uses libheif 1.23.1 with its x265 encoder in lossless
mode. Build it with a C compiler and libheif development files:

[source,sh]
----
cc $(pkg-config --cflags libheif) generate.c \
  $(pkg-config --libs libheif) -o generate
./generate synthetic-all-properties.heic
----

The primary image's namespace-aware XMP properties contain Base64 binary
property lists with this decoded structure:

[source,text]
----
h24  { ap = { d = 3, l = 0 },
       ti = [{i=0,t=0.0}, {i=1,t=0.25}, {i=2,t=0.5}, {i=3,t=0.75}] }
solar { ap = { d = 3, l = 0 },
        si = [{i=0,a=-20,z=0}, {i=1,a=15,z=90},
              {i=2,a=55,z=180}, {i=3,a=10,z=270}] }
apr   { d = 3, l = 0 }
----

Fixture record:

* generator: `generate.c` in this directory;
* source artwork: programmatic solid colors, authored for Genkan under the
  repository license;
* byte size: 1,904 bytes;
* SHA-256:
  `1c38aa9d81234a69873d24a81eec13ca94a5fae0f9fabe0cf034f87f31255f00`;
* top-level order: red, green, blue, white; HEIF item IDs 1, 2, 3, 4;
* dimensions: 8 by 8 for every image;
* metadata: XMP MIME item 5 associated only with primary image 1;
* libheif/ImageMagick reference center pixels: red `(254,0,0,255)`, green
  `(0,255,1,255)`, blue `(0,0,254,255)`, and white `(255,255,255,255)`; the
  ImageIO verifier compares them with the intended colors using a tolerance of
  two channel values for decoder color conversion.

`verify-imageio.swift` independently checks this fixture with macOS ImageIO.
The check in
link:https://github.com/darwin67/genkan/actions/runs/34258316408[GitHub Actions
run 34258316408] observed four images in the expected order, dimensions and
metadata placement. Its center pixels were
`(255,0,0,255)`, `(0,255,1,255)`, `(0,0,255,255)`, and `(255,255,255,255)`.

== Independently authored compatibility fixture

`imageio-wallpapper-h24.heic` was authored on macOS by
link:https://github.com/mczachurski/wallpapper/tree/64d6e2b2088c990e0e7ea0deff8710bca93233fa[`mczachurski/wallpapper`
at commit `64d6e2b`], independently of Genkan's format model and prospective
parser. That generator is MIT licensed. The input PNGs were programmatic solid
colors produced by `generate-png-inputs.swift`, using `wallpapper-h24.json` as
the authoring configuration. After checking out the pinned author, reproduce it
on macOS with:

[source,sh]
----
swift generate-png-inputs.swift "$TMPDIR/wallpapper-fixture"
cp wallpapper-h24.json "$TMPDIR/wallpapper-fixture/"
swift build --package-path /path/to/wallpapper \
  --configuration release --arch arm64 --arch x86_64
/path/to/wallpapper/.build/apple/Products/Release/wallpapper \
  -i "$TMPDIR/wallpapper-fixture/wallpapper-h24.json" \
  -o imageio-wallpapper-h24.heic -q 1.0
----

The PNG files and JSON must share a directory because `wallpapper` resolves
image paths relative to its configuration file.

Fixture record:

* byte size: 4,300 bytes;
* SHA-256:
  `2f82da28545f7d26eb79132d918f1b969d50b29044351ce3732197283e41474f`;
* top-level collection order: red, green, blue, white;
* HEIF item IDs in collection order: 1, 3, 4, 5, demonstrating that metadata
  positions are not HEIF item IDs;
* dimensions: 8 by 8 for every image;
* metadata: XMP MIME item 2 associated only with primary image 1;
* decoded `h24`: `{i=0,t=0.0}`, `{i=1,t=0.25}`, `{i=2,t=0.5}`,
  `{i=3,t=0.75}` with embedded appearance `{l=0,d=3}`;
* macOS ImageIO center pixels: `(254,0,0,255)`, `(0,254,0,255)`,
  `(0,0,254,255)`, and `(255,255,255,255)`.

The independent author and `verify-imageio.swift` produced and verified this
evidence in the linked GitHub Actions run. The macOS CI job continues checking
both fixtures so later byte or metadata changes cannot silently invalidate the
recorded evidence.
